A natural emerald is `a precious green gemstone formed in the earth over millions of years as a variety of the mineral beryl`.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerald)

### Key Characteristics

- **Color:** Sourced from trace amounts of chromium or vanadium, the most valuable stones display a vivid, bluish-green to pure green hue.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/what-is-emerald/)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerald)
- **Inclusions ("Jardin"):** Most natural emeralds contain internal flaws and tiny branching inclusions called *jardin* (French for garden), which verify their natural origin.[[1]](https://emeralds.com/education/basic-ways-to-identify-emeralds/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i3_PDBXM4SE&t=51)
- **Hardness:** They rate 7.5 to 8 on the Mohs scale, but their internal fractures make them fragile and require careful daily wear.[[1]](https://www.bluenile.com/gemstones/green-emerald)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerald)
- **Treatments:** Many natural emeralds are oiled or treated with resin to fill surface fractures and improve clarity.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/what-is-emerald/)
- **Origins:** Top-tier stones are primarily mined in [Colombia, Zambia, and Brazil](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/what-is-emerald/) . You can browse collections or purchase certified loose stones via [GemsNY](https://www.gemsny.com/emerald/basic-search) or [The Natural Emerald Company](https://emeralds.com/emeralds/).[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/what-is-emerald/)[[2]](https://www.gemsny.com/emerald/basic-search)[[3]](https://emeralds.com/emeralds/)

If you are looking to buy or design a piece, let me know:

- What **item** are you making (ring, necklace, earrings)?
- What is your **budget** range?
- Do you have a preference for **origin** (like Colombian vs. Zambian)?
